Request cancellation of outstanding allocations from one run

Source: R/lifecycle_functions.R
cancel_project_run.Rd

Cancellation targets queued, running, or unconfirmed tracked allocations, including dependency-blocked jobs without confirmed scheduler termination. It does not delete project data, logs, or completed outputs. Calling this function with dry_run = FALSE immediately sends cancellation requests to the configured scheduler, so preview the commands first. A successful client exit confirms only the request, not that all allocation processes have stopped. Tracking remains unchanged until scheduler accounting confirms failure/cancellation through reconcile_project_jobs() or the next relevant live run_project() preflight. Concurrent worker completion is preserved. Missing accounting never establishes termination.

Usage

cancel_project_run(input = getwd(), run_id = "latest", dry_run = TRUE)

Arguments

input

A project configuration object, YAML file, or project directory. Defaults to the current working directory.

run_id

Run ID returned by run_project() or listed in inspect_project(input)$runs. An explicit ID is recommended for cancellation.

dry_run

If TRUE, report the commands without contacting the scheduler. If FALSE, request cancellation immediately.

Value

A data frame describing each cancellation attempt. status is would_cancel for previews, cancellation_requested for successful client requests, and failed for client errors. Requests do not mark SQLite rows CANCELLED or authorize immediate duplicate launches.

See also

inspect_project() to inspect current job states before cancellation.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
cancel_project_run(scfg, run$run_id, dry_run = TRUE)
cancel_project_run(scfg, run$run_id, dry_run = FALSE)
} # }
